title: One short of the next doubling
hook: Add up the doubling blocks 1 to 128. The total hides right next to a number you know.
misconception: The total of the doubling blocks is some unpredictable big number, not tied to the next block.
objective: The learner can explain that adding one unit to 1 + 2 + ... + 128 makes a pile that doubles into each block in turn, reaching 256, so the sum is 255, and that the pattern 2^n - 1 holds for any number of doublings.

claims.source: Recomputed with node; the stage's question and reveal use the same SIZES array and TOTAL it draws from.

claims.text: Blocks of 1, 2, 4 ... 128 cells fit inside a 16 by 16 square (256 cells) with exactly one cell left empty.
claims.source: Construction in layout(): each block takes half of the remaining rectangle, so after 8 halvings a 1-cell region is left; 256 - 255 = 1.

claims.text: Adding one unit to the pile doubles it to the size of each next block in turn: 1+1 = 2, 2+2 = 4, ..., 128+128 = 256.
claims.source: Induction: if the pile is 2^k it joins block 2^k to make 2^(k+1).
Geometric series, or the merge argument above by induction on n.

recall.question: What is 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 16 + 32?
recall.why: Add one unit and it doubles through every block: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. So the blocks alone are 64 - 1 = 63.
